narratives.Description: release preflight env poisons task check unit suite (DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT + DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT)
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`task release` Step 5 (`runReleaseCheck` / `releaseCheckEnv`) injects `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1` and `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT=1` into the `task check` subprocess. Those env vars leak into vitest, so branch-gate and cache-staleness unit tests assert the opposite of what the env forces and fail (12 failures observed on the v0.75.0 cut).

## Symptoms

On Windows-native (and likely any host) during production `task release` / `directive release`:

- `verify-branch` / policy resolve tests see `source=env-bypass` and return allow instead of block
- `preflight-cache/evaluate` staleness tests return code 0 instead of 1 because `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT` short-circuits age checks

Standalone `task check` (without those env vars) is green.

## Workaround used for v0.75.0

Ran `task check` green outside release, then `directive release 0.75.0 --skip-ci`.

## Recommended fix

Strip (or never inject) release bypass envs for the **test lane** inside `check:framework-source` / vitest, while keeping them for release git commit --trailer "Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>"/tag steps and for live `verify:cache-fresh` if needed. Mirror the anti-pattern already documented in `deft-directive-release` SKILL.md (do not export `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1` for the entire session).

## Acceptance

- `task release` Step 5 can run full `task check` without `--skip-ci` while bypass envs remain available for commit/tag steps
- Existing unit tests that assert fail-closed branch policy and cache staleness stay green under release preflight
